title: Devrim Mutfağı
author: Bengi Başaran, Umur Talu
description: The Revolutionary Kitchen explores the lives of revolutionaries through the lens of food—what they ate, what they refused to eat, and how their tables reflected their ideologies, contradictions, and humanity. Moving beyond manifestos and battlefields, the book uncovers the personal kitchens of figures such as Lenin, Mao, Castro, Napoleon, Atatürk, Behice Boran, and Deniz Gezmiş, revealing how power, memory, and identity are intertwined with the act of eating. Blending meticulous research with vivid storytelling, it offers both cultural history and intimate recipes—from Lenin’s milk soup to Atatürk’s spinach pastry—transforming them into political and emotional artefacts.
